distractors.reason: We don't say 'work strictly' to mean 'work hard'. 'Strictly' means 'following rules exactly', as in 'strictly confidential'.
'Hardly' means 'almost not'. 'I hardly work' means you rarely work, the opposite of the intended meaning.
'Strongly' is used with verbs such as 'believe' or 'recommend' (strongly believe), not with 'work'.

example_sentence: If you want a good job in the future, you have to ___ hard.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden colocar el adverbio antes del verbo, diciendo 'I hard work' o 'I hardly work' en lugar de 'I work hard'. En inglés el adverbio va después del verbo. Además, 'hardly' parece cognado de 'duro', pero significa 'casi no'.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb it modifies. 'Work hard' means to put a lot of effort into your job or studies. The adverb 'hard' describes the intensity of the action.

related_collocations.example: She studied hard for the certification exam.
Please listen carefully to the instructions.
Many professionals need to speak fluently in English.

memory_tip: WORK + HARD = great effort | HARDLY = almost never (the trap!) | Adverb goes AFTER the verb
